headline: Wallingford police seek SUV after 11-year-old bicyclist is seriously hurt in hit-and-run
dek: The girl was found unconscious at Washington and Hosford streets after a vehicle struck her bicycle and fled; investigators have not identified the driver or released an update on her condition.
body: Wallingford police are searching for a driver after an 11-year-old girl riding a bicycle was seriously injured in a hit-and-run Monday afternoon. Officers responded around 4:20 p.m. Oct. 12 to Washington Street and Hosford Street after receiving a report that a young bicyclist had been struck, according to [NBC Connecticut’s report](https://www.nbcconnecticut.com/news/local/11-year-old-riding-bicycle-seriously-injured-in-wallingford-hit-and-run/3784464/), which attributed the details to police.

Investigators found the girl unconscious and suffering from serious injuries, NBC Connecticut reported. Wallingford firefighters transported her to a hospital for treatment. Police have not publicly released her name or provided a later account of her medical condition, so the extent of her injuries and her recovery remain unknown.

The vehicle is described as a possibly older-model SUV that was traveling south on Washington Street. [The Connecticut Insider](https://www.ctinsider.com/recordjournal/article/wallingford-washington-st-hit-and-run-girl-on-bike-22474753.php) reported that police were looking for a dark-colored SUV, possibly black or gray. The vehicle left the scene after the collision, and police have not announced a license plate, an identified owner or an arrest.

The South-Central Traffic Unit is handling the investigation. Officer Anthony Duhamel is asking anyone who saw the crash, observed the vehicle or knows who was driving to call 203-294-2669. Tips can also be submitted anonymously through the [Wallingford Police Department’s website](https://police.wallingfordct.gov/). The department has not said whether investigators have located surveillance video or identified a specific make and model.

The intersection was closed while officers documented the scene and later reopened, according to Connecticut Insider. That closure was a short-term traffic consequence; the larger public-safety issue is the uncertainty created when a driver leaves after a serious collision. Investigators need witnesses and video from nearby homes, businesses, passing vehicles and doorbell cameras to establish what happened before and after the impact.

Police have released only a preliminary description of the crash. It is not yet known how fast the SUV was traveling, where in the intersection the bicycle was struck, whether the girl was in a marked crossing or bike facility, or whether road, lighting or visibility conditions contributed. Those questions should not be treated as conclusions about responsibility while the investigation is active.

The case also illustrates why early hit-and-run reports can change as investigators collect physical evidence and video. A vehicle description supplied shortly after a crash may be incomplete, and a witness may remember color, body style or direction differently from another observer. The current police request is for information, not an accusation against a particular person or vehicle.

For now, Wallingford police have confirmed the location, the child’s serious injuries, the fleeing vehicle and the active search, but not the child’s current condition or a suspect’s identity. Anyone with relevant information should contact Officer Duhamel or use the department’s anonymous tip channel rather than posting unverified names or claims publicly. NorthEast News will treat any future arrest, charging decision or medical update as a separate development requiring confirmation.
location: Washington Street and Hosford Street, Wallingford, Connecticut
author: NorthEast News Desk
seoTitle: Wallingford police seek SUV in child bicyclist hit-and-run
seoDescription: Wallingford police are seeking an older-model SUV after an 11-year-old bicyclist was seriously injured and left unconscious at Washington and Hosford streets.
